verdict.rationale: vLLM is a self-hosted inference engine. It installs via pip/uv or an official Docker image and runs on the user's own GPUs/CPUs, so prompts and outputs can stay on user-controlled infrastructure rather than going to a vendor that might train on them. However, this protection is only implied by the deployment model; no document explicitly states a no-training or data-handling policy. Missing for 10: explicit first-party statement that user data is never collected or used for training, documentation of telemetry/usage-stats behavior and how to disable it, independent corroboration of the privacy posture.
